headline: 382 yards, 30 allowed, and a noon kick that isn't a bye
dek: Kansas City finally cashed the passing game in a 33-30 overtime grind against Indianapolis; the first road trip of 2026 is Miami on CBS, where a double-digit favorite still has to prove the defense heard its own film session.
videoHook: We're 2-0, we just dropped 523 yards on Sunday night, and we still needed overtime. If you think Miami is a rest week, you haven't sat in Spags' meeting.
theEdge: ESPN FPI posts Kansas City at 85.3 percent and DraftKings lays the Chiefs -10.5 on a 45.5 total, but Polymarketâs 7.6 percent Super Bowl ticket and 16.5 percent AFC ticket still treat 2-0 as a start, not a coronation â especially after a 30-point night the defense already admitted was too loud.

storyline.lede: Two weeks, two identities, one unbeaten: Kansas City bludgeoned Denver on the ground, then had to throw Indianapolis off the field, and Patrick Mahomes answered with 382 yards and three scores in a 33-30 overtime win that still left Steve Spagnuolo staring at 30 points, 329 yards, and 24 first downs. That is the real 2-0 tape. The market has already moved on to Miami as a mismatch â ESPN FPI at 85.3 percent, DraftKings at Chiefs -10.5 â but the next Sunday is the first plane ride of the year, a noon CBS kick at Hard Rock, and a winless Dolphins club with nothing to protect except pride. The Chiefs have more than one way to win. They have not yet shown they can put a messy defensive night in the overhead bin and leave with 3-0.
body: Eric Bieniemyâs downhill identity survived contact. Kenneth Walker III followed a 220-yard team rushing night against Denver with 24 carries for 117 against a Colts front that had already seen the tape, and Mahomes said out loud that defenses are starting to respect the run. That respect is the whole point. Indianapolis loaded up, Kansas City still ran it, and the passing game finally cashed: Travis Kelce went 9 for 101 and a touchdown, Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals finished from the 1, and the offense piled up 523 yards, 29 first downs, 37:00 of clock, and zero turnovers. That is complementary football. It is also how you still need overtime â 5-of-13 on third down kept the Colts in a game the yardage said should have been over.

The other side of the ball is the open question on the flight to Miami. Nick Boltonâs 13 tackles were a volume stat, not a flex: Daniel Jones hit Tyler Warren from a yard out, Jonathan Taylor ripped a 24-yard touchdown, Spencer Shrader twice from 40-plus, and Kansas City never got the night put away. Spagnuolo is not pretending otherwise. Arrowhead Pride reported that it was not lost on the defense that they did not play well, and that honesty is useful with three straight AFC games on the docket, two of them against division rivals after this trip. A 2-0 start that can win with 220 on the ground or 382 through the air is the most complete look this roster has given since the 6-11 hangover. A 2-0 start that needs overtime after 523 yards is also a club that can get surprised at noon if it believes the power rankings.

Miami is being billed as a trap for a reason. The Dolphins are winless and widely treated as the leagueâs worst team; Kansas City has taken the last five in the series and is one of eight 2-0 clubs chasing 3-0. None of that shows up as a bye on the call sheet. Hard Rock in late September is heat, noise when the visitors stall, and a home underdog that will spin the rush and hunt explosives. Chamarri Conner easing back into the secondary is the right piece at the right time if the snap count is real, and Nohl Williams has played like a corner you can live with on the island, but this staff cannot ask a recovering nickel and a young perimeter to cover up another 24-first-down night. The assignment is professional: run Walker until Miamiâs linebackers creep, let Mahomes work play-action and the seams, and make the Dolphins drive the length of the field against a Cover-2 shell instead of scheming them a shot. Finish third down. Leave with 3-0. Then start talking about Las Vegas.

lastGameReview.label: Week 2 Â· Mon Sep 21
lastGameReview.lede: Sunday night at Arrowhead became a 33-30 overtime grind after Indianapolis punched first on a Tyler Warren 1-yard touchdown from Daniel Jones and kept answering with Spencer Shrader field goals and a Jonathan Taylor 24-yard run. Kansas City won the math â 523 yards, 29 first downs, 37:00 of possession, zero turnovers â behind Patrick Mahomes (32-of-47, 382, three touchdowns), Kenneth Walker III (24 for 117), and Travis Kelce (9 for 101 and a score), but the Chiefs still needed extra time because 5-of-13 on third down and a 30-point defensive night never let the Colts feel the game was over.
analysis: The Denver tape dictated Indianapolisâ first adjustment, and Mahomes saw it. After 220 rushing yards in the opener, the Colts had to honor Walker, and Bieniemy still handed it to him 24 times. That is not stubbornness; that is how you keep the play-action fake honest. Once the box got crowded, Mahomes stopped living in the modest 15-of-27 opener and attacked: 47 dropbacks, 382 yards, Kelce as the chain-mover and the 13-yard touchdown, Worthy and Royals finishing on the goal line. Rashee Riceâs early explosive, set up by the Week 1 look opposing coordinators already had to answer, told the rest of the skill room the vertical shots were live. Complementary offense, finally on one card.

The red zone, which owed this team touchdowns through the preseason and the Seattle dress rehearsal, paid. Three Mahomes scores â Kelce from 13, Worthy from the 1, Royals from the 1 â are the difference between a 33-point night and another field-goal slog. Harrison Butkerâs 46-yarder kept the first quarter from getting away after Warrenâs opening touchdown, but the identity shift that matters is finishing. When you run it 24 times and throw it 47, you are asking the OL to win two games; they did enough that Mahomes was never hunting from a turnover hole.

Third down is why 523 yards became overtime. Five conversions in 13 tries means too many punts and too many Shrader possessions. Indianapolis was only 5-of-12 itself and still posted 24 first downs and 329 yards because Kansas City leaked explosives: Warren on the opening script, Taylorâs 24-yard burst right before half, two long Shrader makes. Bolton logging 13 tackles is the linebacker level telling on the front. You do not tackle 13 times in a win unless the defense is living in a firehose. Spagnuoloâs self-scout this week writes itself â points, yards, first downs, all too loud for a club that just became a 10-point road favorite.

Give Shane Steichen and the Colts their due. They did not flinch after Kelce answered, they won the hidden yards with Shrader from 42 and 49, and they made a 2-0 favorite throw 47 times and still walk into overtime. Kansas Cityâs one-score win did not feel like the lucky escapes of past years â 523 yards and zero giveaways is a sustainable profile â but it also did not feel like a team that can sleepwalk into Hard Rock. The pass cashed. The run held up. The defense has to catch the plane with a shorter memory and a tighter call sheet.

takeaways.title: The run forced the throw, and the throw finally cashed
takeaways.body: Walkerâs 24-117 kept the Colts honest after Denverâs 220-yard warning. Mahomes turned that respect into 382 yards and three scores instead of another 15-of-27 night. That is the Bieniemy-Mahomes partnership this roster has been selling since camp.

takeaways.title: Red-zone finishes covered for third-down stalls
takeaways.body: Worthy, Royals, and Kelce punching touchdowns is the correction this offense needed. It does not erase 5-of-13 on third down, which is how a 523-yard game still required overtime. Miamiâs underdog rush will live on those third-and-longs if Kansas City repeats the math.

takeaways.title: Thirty points is a film session, not a footnote
takeaways.body: Boltonâs 13 tackles, Taylorâs 24-yard cut, and 24 Colts first downs are the same story: the defense was on the field too much and too far downfield. Spagnuolo already said it was not good enough. The first road game is a bad week to argue with him.

whatWorked: Walker as a 24-carry feature that still gained 117 against a front that had seen the Denver tape
Mahomes volume passing (32-of-47, 382, 3 TD) once Indianapolis loaded the box
Kelce as both chain-mover (9-101) and red-zone closer (13-yard TD)
Goal-line finishes from Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals after a preseason of field-goal offense
Zero turnovers, 37:00 of possession, and 29 first downs â the game was never out of Kansas Cityâs hands
whatDidnt: Third-down offense at 5-of-13, the hidden reason 523 yards needed overtime
Explosive leakage: Warrenâs opening 1-yard TD and Taylorâs 24-yard score
Two Shrader makes from 42 and 49 that kept Indianapolis on the right side of a one-score script
A 30-point, 24-first-down defensive night Spagnuolo has already called below the standard
Too many Bolton volume tackles, a tell that the second level was chasing instead of dictating

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 2-0 with a ground knockout and a passing grind in the bank, one of eight unbeaten teams and one of four in the AFC, and the next step is the one 2-0 clubs botch: a road noon game against a winless opponent the ticket prices as a mismatch. The offense has proven it can win more than one way. The defense has proven it can survive a loud night. Neither proof is the same as 3-0 in Miami.

workOn.title: Third-down offense has to stop donating possessions
workOn.body: Five-of-13 against Indianapolis is how a 523-yard tape becomes overtime. A desperate Dolphins pass rush in the heat will tee off on 3rd-and-7. Stay on schedule with Walker, then keep the easy-offense answers (boots, screens, Kelce) in the call sheet so Mahomes is not hunting from third-and-long on the road.

workOn.title: Defensive explosives and first-down leakage
workOn.body: Thirty points, 329 yards, and 24 first downs were not a fluke of SNF variance â Spagnuoloâs room already owned it. Miami does not need a complete offense to ruin a trap-game script; it needs one shot and one broken tackle. Two-deep shells and simulated pressure have to replace the firehose Bolton lived in Sunday.

workOn.title: Road operational cleanliness
workOn.body: First plane of 2026, noon CBS, humidity, double-digit favorite. That is how you get a slow start like the Warren touchdown drive and spend the rest of the afternoon climbing. The Chiefs have taken the last five in this series; none of those wins will snap for them if the first 15 minutes in Hard Rock look like the first 15 against Indianapolis.

workOn.title: Secondary snap counts while Conner eases back
workOn.body: Chamarri Connerâs return is timed for this exact week, but easing back is not the same as a full island. Nohl Williams has earned more work. The call sheet has to protect the nickel with coverage shells instead of asking a recovering piece to erase Miamiâs first explosive.

thinkAbout.title: Do you script like a 10.5-point favorite or like a team that just allowed 30?
thinkAbout.body: DraftKings laying Kansas City -10.5 will tempt Andy Reid to sit on a lead. The Colts tape says the lead is not real until third down and the explosives are gone. The right answer is still Walker downhill and Mahomes aggressive â win by two scores because you earned them, not because you managed the number.

thinkAbout.title: How much 12 personnel versus the Rice/Worthy/Royals shots
thinkAbout.body: Kelce at 9-101 is a reason to live in two-TE looks and bully a winless front. Riceâs explosives and Worthyâs goal-line work are a reason to keep 11 personnel on the card. Bieniemy should let Miamiâs first two series tell him which personnel grouping is getting the box to blink.

thinkAbout.title: Is 2-0 a complete team or a small sample the market still does not trust?
thinkAbout.body: Polymarket at 7.6 percent to win the Super Bowl and 16.5 percent to win the AFC is not pricing a juggernaut. The fan debate on a Tyreek Hill reunion can wait; the football debate is whether this defense can travel and whether the dual identity holds up when the building is not Arrowhead.

gamePlan.lede: First road game of the season, CBS at noon, a winless Dolphins team at Hard Rock that the FPI treats as an 85.3 percent layup and the film treats as a trap. The assignment is to run the same complementary script that beat Indianapolis â Walker until the box is loud, Mahomes when it is â and to put Spagnuoloâs self-scout on the field so 30 points does not become a two-week habit.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City is a 2-0 club that can bludgeon you (Denver) or out-gain you by 200 (Indianapolis). Miami is 0-2, at home, with the heat and the underdog rush as its best friends, and a fanbase already whispering trap. The Chiefs should win the line of scrimmage and the skill-talent gap: Walker versus a front that has not had to stop a 24-carry back of this quality, Mahomes/Kelce versus a secondary that will have to pick its poison once the run is respected. The honest edge for Miami is situational â first Kansas City road trip, noon kick after an overtime SNF, Conner easing back, Felix Anudike-Uzomah popping up with a quad â and any explosive the Dolphins can steal before Kansas Cityâs call sheet settles. Give Miami the desperation and the building. Do not give them the first 15 minutes.

keys.title: Open downhill and make Miamiâs linebackers declare
keys.body: Walkerâs 24-117 is the best play-action off-switch Mahomes has had in two years of questions. Inside zone on first down forces Miami to creep, which is when the boot and the seams come due. If Kansas City gets cute and throws empty on the first series, the trap has already started.

keys.title: Finish third down so the defense can play with a lead
keys.body: The Colts night was 523 yards and still overtime because of 5-of-13. Screens, Kelce on the sticks, and designed boots are the answers against a Dolphins rush that will spin to generate a highlight. Stay ahead of the sticks and Spags can live in two-deep instead of chasing.

keys.title: Take away the shot, then rally
keys.body: Indianapolisâ damage was explosives and volume, not a surgical 12-play clinic. Cover-2 early, zone-blitz on obvious dropbacks, and make Miami drive the field against Bolton and a secondary that is adding Conner back in pieces. One broken tackle in the open field is how a 10.5-point favorite becomes a late-window panic.

keys.title: Protect the nickel and the edge while the injury report settles
keys.body: Conner easing back and FAUâs quad mean Spagnuolo should win with shells and simulated pressure, not with max-man and a four-man that has to pin its ears back for 60 minutes. Nohl Williams can take a true outside snap; do not ask the recovering pieces to cover up a light box.

script: Series 1: under-center inside zone to Walker, twice if the first cut gains four â make Miamiâs âbackers walk up in the heat before you show them a pass.
Second-and-medium: play-action boot to Mahomesâ right with Kelce leaking and Worthy on the over; cash the respect the Colts already paid the run.
Keep 12 personnel on the field for a full drive even if it is empty on third down â Kelceâs 9-101 is a mismatch Miami has to bracket, which opens Rice and Royals.
Third-and-4-to-6: spacing screen to Walker rather than another dropback into a spinning rush; the Colts tape says this offense stalls when it hunts hero throws on third down.
Defensively, open in a Cover-2 shell and make Miami throw underneath to Bolton; do not give the building a shot play before Connerâs snap count is real.

On obvious pass, simulated pressure â show six, drop an end, bring a second-level rusher â and let Chris Jones plus the interior collapse the launch point instead of pinning the edge with a thinned FAU rotation.

nextGame.label: Week 3 Â· Sun Sep 27
nextGame.note: First road game of 2026, chasing 3-0 as a 10.5-point favorite in a noon spot already being billed as a trap.

spotlight.title: Noon in Miami is the first 2-0 test that is not about talent
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride already framed Week 3 as a trap: winless Dolphins, double-digit number, first Kansas City road trip after an overtime Sunday nighter. Talent says Chiefs. Situational football says the first 15 minutes will decide whether Hard Rock ever gets a chance to believe.

spotlight.title: The mark they are actually chasing
spotlight.body: Kansas City is one of eight 2-0 teams and one of four unbeaten AFC clubs, joined in the West only by Las Vegas. Getting to 3-0 before the Raiders trip is the first real separator of a season that started under a 6-11 cloud.

spotlight.title: This 2-0 tape has more than one way to win
spotlight.body: Denver was 220 rush yards. Indianapolis was 382 from Mahomes with Walker still at 117. That dual look is the most complete this roster has played since the hangover. Miami is where they prove it travels, not just that it exists at Arrowhead.

spotlight.title: The defense already graded its own film
spotlight.body: Thirty points, 329 yards, 24 first downs â and Spagnuoloâs room did not hide from it. That honesty is the best news of the bye-less week. The worst news would be treating Miami like a self-scout off-week.

spotlight.title: Connerâs return is timed for the first road secondary
spotlight.body: Kansas City stayed unbeaten without two key starters. Conner easing back this week is the right piece for a building that will try to stress the middle of the field. Easing is the word; the call sheet has to meet him halfway.

spotlight.title: Nohl Williams is playing like the next problem on the edge
spotlight.body: Through two games of Year 2, Williams is outplaying the corners drafted ahead of him and giving Spagnuolo a reason to trust the island. Miamiâs first answer if Conner is on a snap count will be to throw at the other guy. Make them throw at Williams and live with it.

spotlight.title: The explosive was not a one-off â it was installed in Week 1
spotlight.body: Riceâs first 20-plus against Indianapolis was set up by what Denver had already seen. That is Reid/Bieniemy layering, not luck. If Miami sits on Walker, Rice and Worthy are the reason the seams should be open by the second series.

spotlight.title: 85 percent is not a coronation price
spotlight.body: FPI at 85.3 and DraftKings at -10.5 will make the internet call this a buy week. Polymarket still has Kansas City at 7.6 percent to win the Super Bowl. The market is telling you 2-0 has not erased last yearâs questions. Covering 10.5 in Miami is how you start to.

matchups.unit: Chiefs run game vs. Dolphins front
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III / Bieniemy inside zone
matchups.note: Walker just went 24-117 against a Colts front that had watched 220 Denver rush yards. Miami has to stop the first cut or Mahomesâ play-action night writes itself again.

matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice
matchups.note: Kelceâs 9-101 forced brackets; Riceâs explosives and Worthyâs finishes punish the leftover. A winless coverage unit cannot double Kelce and still sit on Walker.

matchups.unit: Chiefs OL vs. Dolphins pass rush
matchups.chiefs: Kansas City offensive line, Walker as checkdown
matchups.note: Forty-seven dropbacks against Indianapolis is a heavy ask in humidity. If FAUâs quad thins the other sideâs pass-rush rotation, this becomes a field-position fight: Kansas City must stay on schedule so it is not 3rd-and-long all afternoon.
The Colts just posted 24 first downs and a 24-yard Taylor TD. Miami does not need volume; it needs one leak. Until Kansas City proves the self-scout, this is not a clean KC edge.
Williams has earned the outside. Connerâs return is the right timing if the snap count is real. Shells over man keep this an edge instead of a referendum on a recovering nickel.

matchups.unit: Hidden yards / clock vs. Dolphins desperation
matchups.opponent: Home underdog, heat, crowd on stalled drives
matchups.note: Kansas City has won the last five in this series and just sat on the ball for 37 minutes. The Dolphinsâ path is a short field and a takeaway. Do not donate either.

xsandos.title: Walker one-cut, first-series identity
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, opening script at Hard Rock vs. a winless Dolphins front that has heard -10.5 all week
xsandos.why: Bieniemyâs downhill identity survived Indianapolis after Denverâs 220-yard warning; Walker still got 24 for 117 against a loaded box. Miamiâs only chance to make this a trap is to pin its ears back on first down. Inside zone makes the âbackers declare in the humidity before Mahomes ever has to hunt.
xsandos.coaching: Walker: one cut, no bounce into the boundary on a noon grass/heat game. The OL wins the first step so Kansas City is not 2nd-and-9 on the road. Reid should keep this call on the card even after the first completion â the Colts tape says the run is what opens the rest.

xsandos.title: Boot the respect they just paid Walker
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 after an inside-zone gain, Miami creeping a linebacker into the box
xsandos.why: Mahomes already said he could see Indianapolis loading up after the Broncos rush tape. If Miami copies that â and every 0-2 home underdog will â the boot puts him on the perimeter with Kelce as the easy read and Worthy on the over. This is how 117 rushing yards become 382 passing yards again.
xsandos.coaching: Same zone steps as the run; do not tip the boot with a high hat. Mahomesâ first look is Kelce leaking, second is the deep over. Get it out before Hard Rock can get loud on a held ball. Bieniemy should script this as the second-series answer, not a third-down panic.

xsandos.title: Seams vs. a Cover-3 steal
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-5, max protect, Miami sitting two-high or Cover 3 to steal the run after Walkerâs early carries
xsandos.why: Week 2 produced the 20-plus-yard shots after Riceâs Week 1 setup, and Mahomes just threw for 382. A Dolphins defense trying to bracket Kelce and stop Walker will leave the deep middle soft. Worthy and Royals occupy the corners; Kelce and Rice bend the seams. This is the call that turns a trap-game stalemate into a two-score road lead.
xsandos.coaching: Seams bend to the hash and do not stop. Mahomes throws the window, not the jersey. Worthy has to win on the boundary so the middle hole is real â the same finishing mindset he showed on the 1-yard TD against Indianapolis.

xsandos.title: Easy offense on the sticks
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-4, Miami spinning the rush as a home underdog after Kansas Cityâs 5-of-13 third-down tape
xsandos.why: Five-of-13 on third down is how 523 yards still needed overtime. Miami will hunt the same dropback. Walker as a screen outlet â OL leading in space â keeps Mahomes from another 47-attempt grind in the heat and keeps Spagnuoloâs defense off the field while Conner eases back.
xsandos.coaching: Set the rusher upfield, Walker north-south, no dance. The tackles have to finish in space the way they did as a 37:00 offense against Indianapolis. This is Reidâs âdonât get cute on the roadâ call when the first two dropbacks are dirty.

xsandos.title: Two-deep until the nickel is real
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, early Miami series, Conner on a managed snap count in his return week
xsandos.why: Spagnuolo already owned the 30 points, 329 yards, and 24 first downs. Two-deep takes away the shot that lets a trap-game crowd believe, and it lets Bolton rally after a 13-tackle firehose night. Conner easing back is the right piece only if Kansas City does not ask him to play island man on the first drive.
xsandos.coaching: Corners squat and tackle; safeties split the posts. Nohl Williams stays disciplined on the outside â he has earned that trust â and Bolton fits the under. Make Miami drive the length of Hard Rock instead of scheming the Taylor-style explosive Kansas City just gave up.

xsandos.title: Show six, drop the end, rattle the launch point
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-7-plus, Miami in obvious dropback, Kansas City protecting a lead or escaping a slow start
xsandos.why: Indianapolis converted only 5-of-12 and still scored 30 because Kansas City never got off the field on schedule. Simulated pressure â show heat, drop a lineman, rush the second level â is Spagsâ way to rattle a winless offense without exposing Conner and Williams to free access. Interior collapse from Chris Jones, with Omarr Norman-Lott as the reminder piece, is how you end drives without pinning a thinned FAU edge for 60 minutes.
xsandos.coaching: Sell the six-man look, drop the end into the hook, add Bolton or the nickel as the rusher. Jones has to wreck the launch point so the zone behind it is not a layup. Do not blitz empty and leave Williams on an island if Miami motions into it â the Colts tape says the explosive, not the conversion rate, is what kills you.

coaching.topic: Steve Spagnuoloâs self-scout vs. the trap script
coaching.detail: Spags has already told the building the 30-point night was not good enough. The coaching win in Miami is a quieter call sheet â two-deep early, simulated pressure late â not a revenge four-man that asks a recovering nickel to cover up another 24 first downs.

The OC has the look he wanted: Walker as a 24-carry hammer, Mahomes as the 382-yard closer once the box is loud. Script the same order on the road. If he opens empty to âget aheadâ of a 10.5, he is playing the number instead of the Colts tape.

Reid has taken the last five in this series and does not need a statement script. He needs a clean first 15 minutes after an overtime SNF and a noon kick. Manage the heat with 12 personnel and clock, not with a prevent lead that Indianapolis already proved can leak.

coaching.topic: Miami as a desperate home underdog
coaching.detail: Give the Dolphins the building, the heat, and the nothing-to-lose rush. The staff that loses this game is the one that confuses FPIâs 85.3 percent with a bye week and lets one explosive become a second-half problem.

injuries.note: Thursday report framed Conner as easing back for the Miami trip, the first real secondary reinforcement of a 2-0 start that has been missing key starters.
FAU popped up with a quad on the Wednesday report heading into Miami, a problem for a pass-rush rotation Spagnuolo may need if Kansas City has to protect a lead on the road.

personnel.move: Connerâs snap-count return in the nickel
personnel.detail: Kansas City stayed unbeaten without two key starters; Conner easing back this week is the right piece for a road secondary if Spags protects him with shells instead of max-man.

personnel.move: Nohl Williams as a true outside answer
personnel.detail: Williams is outplaying corners drafted ahead of him through two games of Year 2. If Conner is on a pitch count, Williams is the island, not the excuse.

personnel.move: Walker as the feature, not a committee afterthought
personnel.detail: Twenty-four carries for 117 after a 220-yard team night in Week 1 is a feature back. Miami is not the week to get cute with the split if the box is light.

A second-round tackle who looked like a reach a year ago is exactly the kind of interior reminder you want if the edge rotation is dealing with a quad and the call is simulated pressure, not four-man hope.

strategies: Open the game under center with Walker inside zone and do not come off it until Miamiâs linebackers are in the box.
Boot Mahomes off that run fake with Kelce as the first read â cash the respect Indianapolis already paid.
Live in 12 personnel for a full series even on the road; Kelceâs 9-101 is the mismatch that creates Rice/Worthy explosives.
Third-and-medium: screen to Walker rather than another 47-dropback night in the humidity.
Defense: Cover-2 early to erase the shot play, then zone-blitz on obvious pass so Connerâs return week is not an island referendum.
If you get a two-score lead, keep running it â the Colts tape says prevent football and 5-of-13 third downs is how favorites donate overtime.
debates: Is Miami actually a trap, or is that just what 2-0 teams tell themselves before they cover 10.5?
Should Reid keep throwing if theyâre up two scores, or does the Colts overtime tape argue against ever sitting on a lead?
Is the defense a 30-point problem or a one-night leak that Spagsâ self-scout already fixed?
Do you want more Walker at 24 carries, or is it time to let Rice/Worthy/Royals hunt explosives every series?
Is the Tyreek reunion noise a real roster conversation, or a distraction from a skill room that just produced 382 yards without him?

runOfShow.segment: Cold open / the number vs. the tape
runOfShow.talkTrack: 2-0, 523 yards, overtime, and now weâre a 10.5-point road favorite at noon. If you think Miami is a bye, you didnât watch Spagsâ film. Thatâs the show.

runOfShow.segment: Last game film: how 382 still needed OT
runOfShow.talkTrack: Walk the Colts tape: Walker 24-117 against a loaded box, Mahomes 32-of-47 for 382, Kelce 9-101, Worthy and Royals from the 1. Then the other tape: 5-of-13, Warrenâs opener, Taylorâs 24-yarder, Boltonâs 13 tackles, 30 points. Complementary offense, incomplete defense.

One of eight unbeaten, chasing 3-0, first plane of the year. Dual identity is real. Third down and explosives are the fixes. Conner easing back, FAUâs quad, Williams playing like a No. 1. Polymarket still at 7.6 percent â the league is not convinced.

runOfShow.segment: Miami game plan and trap framing
runOfShow.talkTrack: Give the Dolphins the building and the desperation. Script Walker, boot Mahomes, live in 12, screen on third-and-4. Defense in two-deep until the nickel is real, zone-blitz on obvious pass. Cover 10.5 by earning two scores, not by managing the number.

Six calls: inside zone, play-action boot, four verts, Walker screen, Cover-2 shell, simulated pressure. Tie each one to Walkerâs respect, Kelceâs 101, Connerâs snap count, and the Colts explosives we cannot give Miami.

Walker vs. that front is ours. Spags vs. explosives is a PUSH until proven. Conner easing, FAU quad, Williams on the island. Trap or mismatch? Sit on the lead or keep throwing? Tyreek noise vs. the room that just threw for 382.
Leave Hard Rock 3-0, then we talk about Las Vegas on the road. If we donate a shot play at noon, weâre going to spend a week explaining a loss nobodyâs model saw. See you Sunday morning.
